canon-exit-gate ran its own fresh, independent check on SPEC-APPLY-BATCH-002 (same file, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gabe-Projects-callisto/ae412d01-e061-4047-918b-0d1df3d4d118/scratchpad/SPEC-APPLY-BATCH-002.json). Good news: it independently re-verified the persist-trigger fix and AC-015 are both genuinely sound (re-derived the logic itself against apply.rs and the path-normalization chain, not just trusting the prior rounds). But it found 3 new blockers elsewhere that earlier rounds missed. Verdict: FAIL, retry_count 0 (first exit-gate submission) — please make one more revision to the SAME file.

## Blocker 1: AC-005's fixture is self-contradictory and cannot detect the bug it exists to catch

AC-005's fixture is "one plain, non-inherited dependency and one workspace-inherited dependency, both rewritten" — that produces exactly ONE Manifest-trait entry targeting P (the plain dep; the inherited one routes to DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency, not DepWriteTarget::Manifest). So "the count for P equals the number of Manifest-trait entries targeting P" evaluates to 1 — but the criterion's own point is to prove batching did NOT engage, i.e. it wants to show the count is "not 1" in the batching-would-give sense. With only one Manifest entry, open_call_count is 1 whether the exclusion guard works correctly OR is completely absent/broken — the test can't distinguish a correct implementation from a buggy one. This is the same "test that can't fail" defect class this whole session has been vigilant about (recall the T14-T20 red-phase-waived-task discipline in Spec A).

Fix: require the fixture to carry at least TWO plain, non-inherited dependency rewrites on P (two DepWriteTarget::Manifest entries) PLUS the one workspace-inherited rewrite (DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency{root_manifest: P}). Assert open_call_count() == 2 for P, with explicit text stating that a WRONGLY-batched implementation would incorrectly yield 1 (proving the assertion is discriminating). Update AC-006 to match — assert both plain deps' new specs plus the inherited dep's new spec in [workspace.dependencies].

## Blocker 2: AC-011 mandates a fixture that cannot be constructed — the ordering claim is provably false

AC-011 requires a fixture where applying the rewrite before the bump is "observably wrong" in the final bytes. The exit-gate read CargoToml::update_dependency_spec and CargoToml::write_version end to end: write_version writes [package].version; update_dependency_spec writes a dependencies-table entry using DepSpec::render() of a value that's a CONSTANT carried in SpecRewrite.to (precomputed in the plan, never read from the manifest at apply time). update_dependency_spec never reads the manifest's version. So the two mutations touch disjoint CST locations with plan-constant values — they are commutative. Even your "self-referencing pin" construction (rewriting a sibling dep to the bump's target_version) doesn't help, because the pinned string is already baked into the plan before apply_version_plan ever runs — it's not derived at apply time from whatever the bump did. No fixture can make bump-before-rewrites byte-observable, because it genuinely isn't, given how these two mutators work. Verify this yourself by re-reading both functions.

Fix: split AC-011 into two criteria. (a) Rewrite-internal ordering (genuinely byte-observable): mandate two SpecRewrite entries with the SAME RewriteKey (same target P, same dependency name, same kind) and DIFFERENT `to` values in plan.rewrites order; assert the final on-disk spec equals the SECOND one's value — this is only true if rewrite_indices is applied in plan.rewrites order, so it's a real, satisfiable test. (b) Bump-before-rewrites ordering is NOT byte-observable given the current mutators — don't try to prove it via output bytes. Instead ground it in the failure/skip paths that already prove sequencing exists: AC-014 (bump precondition failure means update_dependency_spec is never called — proves bump is checked first) and AC-016 (bump skip branch is evaluated before the rewrite step — proves the same). State explicitly that these two ACs together establish the sequencing guarantee, since no independent byte-level test is possible for the successful-bump-then-successful-rewrite case. If you want a stronger direct proof, consider requiring a call-order recorder/instrumentation in the test rather than an on-disk byte assertion — your call which approach is cleaner.

## Blocker 3: api_surface's ApplyOutcome.staged claim is factually false and leaves a real behavior decision undecided

Your apply_version_plan api_surface entry claims "ApplyOutcome.staged's contents and ordering semantics (one entry per distinct modified path, in the same relative order paths were first encountered) are unchanged." This is wrong on both counts, verified against the real current code:
1. TODAY: modified_paths.push(p.clone()) runs unconditionally per entry (apply.rs:97, apply.rs:122), and outcome.staged = modified_paths is assigned with NO dedup (apply.rs:335; the only contains() guard is for lockfiles at apply.rs:294). So today, N Manifest entries targeting the same path P put P into staged N times — "one entry per distinct modified path" describes neither today's actual behavior nor something this spec preserves.
2. AFTER BATCHING: your prescribed `batched: BTreeMap<PathBuf, ManifestWriteGroup>` iterates paths in lexicographic order, not plan-encounter order — so a plan with a bump on "z-crate/Cargo.toml" and a rewrite on "a-crate/Cargo.toml" would yield staged in a DIFFERENT order than today. ApplyOutcome.staged is a public field; no acceptance criterion currently covers it; every retained test uses .contains() so nothing would catch either change. An implementer has no answer to "does a batched path contribute 1 entry or N to staged, and in what order?"

Fix: correct the api_surface text to state TODAY's actual behavior (one push per entry, duplicates possible for a shared path, plan-encounter order). Then explicitly DECIDE the post-batching contract (the exit-gate's suggestion, which seems reasonable: one push per batched group — i.e. deduplicated for batched paths — labeled as a documented behavior change the same way AC-004 documents the all-or-nothing persist change). Add a new acceptance criterion pinning `staged` for the AC-001 multi-entry fixture (P appears exactly once in staged, not N times), and either pin the resulting ordering explicitly or state plainly that ordering is unspecified/not guaranteed for batched vs. mixed-routing paths.

## Non-blocking notes from the gate (use your judgment, not required but worth considering)

1. CargoToml::update_dependency_spec delegates to WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_dependency for a workspace-inherited dep, which loads+writes+persists the ROOT Cargo.toml as a side effect FROM INSIDE a batched group's rewrite step. The gate notes this is only safe because groups are opened/mutated/persisted strictly sequentially and Spec A's AC-017 guarantees no Manifest-routed rewrite is ever for an inherited dep. Consider stating "per-group open→persist sequencing is strictly sequential, one group fully completes before the next group begins" as an explicit requirement rather than leaving it implied by AC-012 — this matters because an implementation that hoisted all opens ahead of the group loop (a plausible "optimization") would reintroduce a stale-handle clobber, the exact bug class that killed the original combined spec.
2. AC-001/AC-002/AC-005 say "the counter... for path P" but the counters are process-global, not per-path — unambiguous given single-path fixtures today, but drop "for path P" for clarity since it could confuse an implementer.
3. Scope at 16 criteria across 2 crates/6 files is at the upper edge of one planning cycle but the gate called it coherent, not a fail reason — no action needed unless the eventual plan runs long, in which case AC-015's cross-crate test is separable.

Please verify all three fixes against the real code yourself (re-read the actual update_dependency_spec/write_version implementations for blocker 2, actual apply.rs:97/122/294/335 for blocker 3) before writing — same rigor as every prior round. Report back what changed.

5. **Missing error handling** — the spec has 4 criteria with is_error_case: true (AC-004, AC-012, AC-014, and check if there are others) — confirm each has a real test/implementation step in its covering task, not just a mention.

Verify T07's implementation/failing_test steps actually encode this constraint concretely enough that an implementer couldn't accidentally hoist all opens ahead of the loop — vague language here would be under-specification given how much this constraint matters (it's what prevents the exact class of bug that killed the original combined spec).

Output your standard JSON issue list (task_id, type, description, suggested_fix) plus an overall pass/fail verdict.

content.text:
Confirmed: `cargo clippy -p callisto-manifests --all-targets -- -D warnings` (the workspace's actual lint gate, per `just lint`) fails on this exact commit's new file. This is a real, reproducible CI-breaking regression, not a style nit.

## Review of commit d2b1014 (T01)

**Status: changes_requested**

### Issues

1. **`crates/callisto-manifests/tests/persist_call_count_test.rs:10`** — `use callisto_manifests::{open, Manifest, OpenContext};` imports `Manifest` but never uses it. `open()` returns `Box<dyn Manifest>`, and trait methods on a `dyn Trait` object are callable without the trait in scope, so the import is dead. Verified two ways: `cargo test -p callisto-manifests --test persist_call_count_test` emits `warning: unused import: \`Manifest\`` and, decisively, `cargo clippy -p callisto-manifests --all-targets -- -D warnings` — the actual command `just lint`/`just ci` runs — **fails to compile** with `error: unused import: \`Manifest\`` / `error: could not compile \`callisto-manifests\` (test "persist_call_count_test") due to 1 previous error`. This is a must_fix: the commit as it stands breaks `just ci`. Fix is a one-line import trim (drop `Manifest` from the `use` list, or reference it e.g. via `let _: &dyn Manifest = &*manifest;` if the plan wants it kept for documentation clarity — trimming is simpler and matches the file's own stated "fully-qualified, minimal" style).

### Verified correct (per the review's specific checks)

- **Success-only increment**: `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs` — `record_persist_call()` is called strictly after `atomic_write(...).map_err(...)?`, so a propagated `Err` never reaches it. Traced and confirmed by reading the diff directly.
- **Dedicated integration binary is genuinely necessary**: `grep` confirms cargo.rs/npm.rs/python.rs's own `#[cfg(test)]` modules contain 93 `#[test]` functions and 30 `.persist(...)` call sites, none tagged `#[serial]`. An in-`--lib` placement of a process-global-counter assertion would race all of them. The plan's rationale (mirroring `crates/callisto-graph/tests/apply_persist_open_count_test.rs`'s documented precedent for `OPEN_CALL_COUNT`) is accurate, not just asserted.
- **Test genuinely proves the property**: `cargo_persist_increments_persist_call_count_on_success` resets the counter, calls the real `open()` → `manifest.persist()` path against a real tempdir file, and asserts the counter is exactly 1 — this would catch a regression (e.g., a future edit that moves `record_persist_call()` before the `?`, or drops it entirely). Ran it: passes standalone.
- **Scope adherence**: exactly the 4 files named in the plan's `files` list, plus `Cargo.lock` (expected, auto-generated by the new dev-dependency). `PackageJson`/`PyprojectToml` are correctly left unwired — T02/T03 exist in the plan and are not silently dropped.
- **serial_test placement**: added alphabetically after `proptest` in `[dev-dependencies]`, matching plan instructions.
- **No other rust-hazards.md taxonomy hits** in the diff: no `unwrap_or*` swallowing, no `map_err(|_|` erasure (the existing `map_err(|e| ... e.to_string())` predates this diff and isn't touched by it), no unsafe, no silent no-op `Ok(())` path.

### Sibling gaps
None beyond the explicitly-deferred, plan-documented ones (`PackageJson::persist`, `PyprojectToml::persist` — covered by T02/T03).

### Error-state coverage gap (standing directive: "great corner case and error state test coverage")
T01 itself doesn't test "a failed persist does not increment the counter" — by design, deferred. But tracing the **whole plan** (not just T01), no later task actually asserts this either: T13/AC-016 only asserts `persist_call_count() == 1` on a *successful* skipped-bump-plus-rewrite scenario, and the one failure-injection test that does exist (the chmod-0o555 P2-persist-failure fixture, `batched_group_rewrite_failure_leaves_bump_and_first_rewrite_unpersisted`) asserts on-disk byte content only — it never reads `persist_call_count()` after the injected failure. The commit message's claim "an Err does not increment it" is proven by code trace, not by any test anywhere in the plan. This isn't a T01 blocker (correctly out of this task's scope), but it is a real coverage gap that appears to be silently dropped from the plan rather than deliberately deferred with a stated reason — worth flagging to whoever owns the plan before AC-002/AC-005/AC-016/AC-018 close out.

### Reasoning (private)
The plan's own text is unusually rigorous (revision history documents exactly this kind of check), and the implementation faithfully follows it — the only actual defect is the dead import, which is a mechanical slip, not a design problem. It's a hard blocker only because this specific repo's CI runs `-D warnings` via clippy on `--all-targets`, which includes integration-test binaries; had `just ci` only run `cargo test` this would just be a warning. I verified this is not a flaky/environment-specific failure — reproduced twice.

### Issues

1. **`crates/callisto-manifests/tests/persist_call_count_test.rs:10`** — `use callisto_manifests::{open, Manifest, OpenContext};` imports `Manifest` but never uses it. `open()` returns `Box<dyn Manifest>`, and trait methods on a `dyn Trait` object are callable without the trait in scope, so the import is dead. Verified two ways: `cargo test -p callisto-manifests --test persist_call_count_test` emits `warning: unused import: \`Manifest\`` and, decisively, `cargo clippy -p callisto-manifests --all-targets -- -D warnings` — the actual command `just lint`/`just ci` runs — **fails to compile** with `error: unused import: \`Manifest\`` / `error: could not compile \`callisto-manifests\` (test "persist_call_count_test") due to 1 previous error`. Fix is a one-line import trim (drop `Manifest` from the `use` list, or reference it e.g. via `let _: &dyn Manifest = &*manifest;` if the plan wants it kept for documentation clarity — trimming is simpler and matches the file's own stated "fully-qualified, minimal" style).

### Verified correct (per the review's specific checks)

- **Success-only increment**: `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs` — `record_persist_call()` is called strictly after `atomic_write(...).map_err(...)?`, so a propagated `Err` never reaches it. Traced and confirmed by reading the diff directly.

An in-`--lib` placement of a process-global-counter assertion would race all of them. The plan's rationale (mirroring `crates/callisto-graph/tests/apply_persist_open_count_test.rs`'s documented precedent for `OPEN_CALL_COUNT`) is accurate, not just asserted.
- **Test genuinely proves the property**: `cargo_persist_increments_persist_call_count_on_success` resets the counter, calls the real `open()` → `manifest.persist()` path against a real tempdir file, and asserts the counter is exactly 1 — this would catch a regression (e.g., a future edit that moves `record_persist_call()` before the `?`, or drops it entirely). Ran it: passes standalone.
- **Scope adherence**: exactly the 4 files named in the plan's `files` list, plus `Cargo.lock` (expected, auto-generated by the new dev-dependency). `PackageJson`/`PyprojectToml` are correctly left unwired — T02/T03 exist in the plan and are not silently dropped.

The plan's own text is unusually rigorous (revision history documents exactly this kind of check), and the implementation faithfully follows it — the only actual defect is the dead import, which is a mechanical slip, not a design problem. - (b) Confirmed: `#[serial_test::serial]` (unkeyed) only mutually excludes *other* `#[serial]`-tagged tests. It does nothing to exclude the ~10+ non-serial siblings in the same file that also call `persist()`. Under plain `cargo test -p callisto-graph` (multi-threaded, single process) — which is exactly what `.moon/tasks/rust.yml`'s `test` task runs, invoked by `moon run :test`, the fallback path in the justfile's `test:` recipe (`cargo nextest run --workspace || moon run :test`) — a non-serial sibling can race the AC-004 test's `reset_persist_call_count()` → `assert_eq!(persist_call_count(), 0, ...)` window and cause a spurious failure.

Based on thorough independent verification, here is my review.

## Verification performed

1. **Targeted test run** (matches the task's own `verify_command`): `cargo test -p callisto-graph --test apply_persist_open_count_test` → `test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed`, including the new `mixed_routing_root_cargo_toml_excludes_plain_dependencies_from_batching`.
2. **Clippy**: `cargo clippy -p callisto-graph --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean, no warnings.
3. **Full crate suite** (`cargo test -p callisto-graph`) was still compiling/running in the background at the time of this report (large crate, many integration test binaries) — the narrower, task-specified verify_command already passed cleanly and clippy already covers `--all-targets` so no new warnings were introduced by this test-only diff.
4. **`#[serial]` presence**: confirmed on all three tests in the file (`apply_version_plan_opens_each_distinct_manifest_path_exactly_once`, `apply_version_plan_batches_open_persist_and_dedupes_staged_for_shared_path`, and the new `mixed_routing_root_cargo_toml_excludes_plain_dependencies_from_batching`) — process-global-counter isolation is intact.
5. **Scope**: `git show ff68896 --stat` confirms exactly one file changed, `crates/callisto-graph/tests/apply_persist_open_count_test.rs`, 89 insertions, 0 deletions — test-only, matching the task description and NO-RED-PHASE justification.
6. **Traced the count-of-2 claim end-to-end** in `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`:
   - `classify_manifest_writes` (line 43) puts `Cargo.toml` into `resolver_routed` because the plan's rewrite has `DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency { root_manifest: "Cargo.toml" }` (line 53) → the path lands in `classification.excluded`, not `batched`.
   - The batched-pass loop (line 136) never touches this path (correctly excluded).
   - The rewrites loop (line 213) hits both `DepWriteTarget::Manifest("Cargo.toml")` entries (plain-a, plain-b); each passes the `excluded.contains(p)` guard (line 216) and calls `open(&decl, &ctx)?` individually — two separate `open` calls, two separate `persist` calls.
   - The `DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency` arm (line 232) calls `WorkspaceCargoResolver::load(&root.join(root_manifest))?` and `ws_res.write_dependency(...)`.
   - Checked `WorkspaceCargoResolver::load` in `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs:527` — it calls `fs::read_to_string` directly and parses via `toml_edit`, **never** calling `callisto_manifests::open` (which is the sole `OPEN_CALL_COUNT.fetch_add` site, `crates/callisto-manifests/src/lib.rs:157`). Same for `write_dependency` (line 651) — it mutates `self.document` in place via `toml_edit`, no `open` call.
   - **Conclusion: confirmed, not merely plausible** — `open_call_count() == 2` is the only possible outcome given this code path; the CargoWorkspaceDependency entry structurally cannot contribute to the counter.

## Findings

No non-negotiable Rust hazard violations found (no unsafe blocks, no `.unwrap_or`/silent fallback, no discarded params, no `map_err(|_|`, no panics outside test code, no integer overflow risk, no duplicate diagnostic codes). Test uses `.unwrap()` throughout, which is acceptable per the hazards reference's false-positive check ("Test code and `fn main` are acceptable").

Test quality: the test asserts both the process-level invariant (`open_call_count() == 2`) and the actual on-disk outcome (all three dependency specs present in the file bytes), so it verifies observable behavior, not just an internal counter — satisfying AC-006 as well as AC-005.

Out of scope for T10/AC-005/AC-006 (which target the rewrite-side CargoWorkspaceDependency case specifically), but worth a follow-up task if the plan intends full symmetric coverage of both mixed-routing directions."

## AC-017: bump-before-rewrites ordering is not byte-observable, correcting T13's commit-message evidence

T13's commit (`1234bef`) recorded a blanket claim that `CargoToml::update_dependency_spec` "only touches a dependency-table entry with a plan-time-constant value, no read of `current_version()`/other state." An independent review of that commit caught that this claim is incomplete for one branch, and since commit messages cannot be corrected after the fact, the complete evidence is recorded here instead.

Read `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs` directly:

- `CargoToml::write_version` (lines 200-242): touches only `[package].version` in the direct-write branch, or does an explicit pinned replacement of that same field for a workspace-inherited member. No other state is read or written. Claim holds without qualification.
- `CargoToml::update_dependency_spec` (lines 290-377): for a **non-inherited** dependency (lines 320-376, the case both of T13's AC-014/AC-016 fixtures and this file's own AC-005/AC-006 fixture exercise), the claim holds exactly as stated -- a disjoint dependency-table entry is mutated with a plan-time-constant `DepSpec`, no read of `current_version()`. For an **inherited** dependency (lines 305-318), the method instead delegates to `WorkspaceCargoResolver::load(&root_cargo)` followed by `ws_res.write_dependency(name, new, permit)` -- an immediate, synchronous read-and-persist against a **different physical file** (the workspace root `Cargo.toml`), not the manifest whose handle `update_dependency_spec` was called on. `WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_dependency` calls `self.persist(permit)` internally (cargo.rs:709), and `WorkspaceCargoResolver::persist` (cargo.rs:715-723) does not call `crate::record_persist_call()`, so this delegated write is invisible to `persist_call_count()`.

This does not weaken AC-017's actual claim: the delegated write lands on a file distinct from the one being batched in the group under discussion, so it has no bearing on whether bump-before-rewrites ordering is byte-observable *within that group's own manifest*. It also does not contradict this spec's own scope: `non_goals` already states that `WorkspaceCargoResolver`-routed writes remain immediate, per-entry, and outside `persist_call_count`'s instrumentation (which is scoped exclusively to the `Manifest` trait's three implementors). The correction here is one of completeness in T13's evidence write-up, not a functional defect in the shipped code -- verified via `cargo test -p callisto-graph --lib apply::tests` (22 passed) and `cargo clippy -p callisto-graph --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean) after this note was added, confirming no code change was needed or made.

+- `CargoToml::write_version` (lines 200-242): touches only `[package].version` in the direct-write branch, or does an explicit pinned replacement of that same field for a workspace-inherited member. No other state is read or written. Claim holds without qualification.

+- `CargoToml::update_dependency_spec` (lines 290-377): for a **non-inherited** dependency (lines 320-376, the case both of T13's AC-014/AC-016 fixtures and this file's own AC-005/AC-006 fixture exercise), the claim holds exactly as stated -- a disjoint dependency-table entry is mutated with a plan-time-constant `DepSpec`, no read of `current_version()`. For an **inherited** dependency (lines 305-318), the method instead delegates to `WorkspaceCargoResolver::load(&root_cargo)` followed by `ws_res.write_dependency(name, new, permit)` -- an immediate, synchronous read-and-persist against a **different physical file** (the workspace root `Cargo.toml`), not the manifest whose handle `update_dependency_spec` was called on. `WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_dependency` calls `self.persist(permit)` internally (cargo.rs:709), and `WorkspaceCargoResolver::persist` (cargo.rs:715-723) does not call `crate::record_persist_call()`, so this delegated write is invisible to `persist_call_count()`.

+This does not weaken AC-017's actual claim: the delegated write lands on a file distinct from the one being batched in the group under discussion, so it has no bearing on whether bump-before-rewrites ordering is byte-observable *within that group's own manifest*. It also does not contradict this spec's own scope: `non_goals` already states that `WorkspaceCargoResolver`-routed writes remain immediate, per-entry, and outside `persist_call_count`'s instrumentation (which is scoped exclusively to the `Manifest` trait's three implementors). The correction here is one of completeness in T13's evidence write-up, not a functional defect in the shipped code -- verified via `cargo test -p callisto-graph --lib apply::tests` (22 passed) and `cargo clippy -p callisto-graph --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean) after this note was added, confirming no code change was needed or made.

## Part 2: AC-017 claim about `CargoToml::update_dependency_spec` — INACCURATE

Full body: `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs:290-377`.

The inherited-dependency delegation branch, `cargo.rs:305-318`, verbatim:

```rust
        if self.inherited_deps.contains(&(kind, name.to_string())) {
            let root_cargo = self.workspace_root.join("Cargo.toml");
            if self.absolute == root_cargo {
                return Err(ManifestError::InvariantViolation {
                    path: self.path.clone(),
                    message: format!(
                        "dependency `{name}` is workspace-inherited but this manifest IS the workspace root (`{}`); refusing to delegate to avoid overwriting the just-written root manifest with a stale in-memory document",
                        root_cargo.display()
                    ),
                });
            }
            let mut ws_res = WorkspaceCargoResolver::load(&root_cargo)?;
            return ws_res.write_dependency(name, new, permit);
        }
```

Answers to the specific questions:

- **Does it write anything outside the member manifest? YES.** `WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_dependency` (cargo.rs:651-713) mutates `[workspace.dependencies].<name>` in the **workspace-root `Cargo.toml`**, then ends with `self.persist(permit)` (line 712), which calls `crate::atomic::atomic_write(&self.absolute_path, …)` (cargo.rs:717). So the branch performs an **immediate, unbatched disk write to a different file** — the root manifest — and returns before ever touching a `dependencies`/`dev-dependencies`/`build-dependencies` table in the member manifest (lines 320–376 are unreachable on this path). The AC-017 phrase "writes only a dependencies/dev-dependencies/build-dependencies table entry" is false for this branch on two counts: wrong file, wrong table, and the write is a `persist`, not a deferred in-memory mutation.

- **Does it read the manifest's current version or any apply-time state?** It does **not** derive the written value from any read — the value written is exactly `new.render()` (cargo.rs:683), where `new` is the parameter passed in, so that half of AC-017 is correct. But it **does** read apply-time on-disk state: `WorkspaceCargoResolver::load(&root_cargo)` (cargo.rs:316 → 527-558) does `fs::read_to_string(root_manifest_path)` and re-parses the root manifest at apply time. That is a read-modify-write cycle against a file that another in-memory handle may have already mutated — the exact staleness hazard the guard at 307–315 partially covers (it only covers the self-referential case where the member *is* the root).

- The branch predicate `self.inherited_deps` is populated at `open()` time (cargo.rs:54-73, stored at line 95), not apply time, so the routing decision itself is not apply-time-derived.

Net: AC-017 is accurate about *value provenance* (never derived from the manifest's current version), inaccurate about *write scope* (the delegation branch escapes the member manifest and persists the workspace root immediately).

## Part 3: AC-017 claim about `CargoToml::write_version` — ACCURATE

`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs:200-242`.

Inherited-member branch, lines 201–218:

```rust
        if self.inherited_version {
            // ... Routing the bump to [workspace.package] would silently change the version for
            // every other workspace member. Instead, write an explicit pinned version directly
            // to this member's [package] section, replacing the workspace-inherited entry with
            // a standalone string value.
            let pkg = self
                .document
                .get_mut("package")
                .and_then(|p| p.as_table_mut())
                .ok_or_else(|| ManifestError::MissingField { path: self.path.clone(), field: "package" })?;
            pkg.insert("version", toml_edit::value(v.render()));
            self.inherited_version = false;
            return Ok(());
        }
```

Both branches touch only `document["package"]["version"]` in the member's own in-memory document, write only `v.render()` (the caller-supplied `Version`), read nothing from disk, and never call `persist` — `_permit` is unused (line 200), and both paths return `Ok(())` without any `atomic_write`. The only extra effect is the in-memory `self.inherited_version = false` bookkeeping at line 216, which changes no file content. No delegation to `WorkspaceCargoResolver` exists on this path, so unlike `update_dependency_spec`, `write_version` genuinely stays within the member manifest.</result>

---
name: feedback-iterate-reviews-in-foreground
description: Multi-round adversarial review loops (spec/plan revision cycles) should run each Agent call in the foreground, not background — background completion notifications were unreliable and confused the user about what was actually running.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When running an iterative revise→re-check loop (e.g. canon-drafter ↔ canon-auditor, or vector-planner ↔ vector-challenger, cycling until a clean pass), dispatch each round's agent with `run_in_background: false` and wait for the direct result, rather than `run_in_background: true` and waiting for a task-notification.

**Why:** During the SPEC-APPLY-BATCH-002 ("Spec B", see [[project_manifest_persist_track]]) canon and vector review cycles, background-dispatched agents repeatedly went idle after finishing their work without proactively sending their final report — the only signal was a bare `idle_notification` with no content, requiring a manual `SendMessage` check-in to actually pull the result out. This happened for essentially every agent in the pipeline (verifier, auditor, drafter, exit-gate, planner, challenger) across dozens of rounds. The user noticed the pattern, called it out twice with increasing frustration ("The ui doesn't show any agents running", "You're full of shit", "Just rerun dammit"), and the fix — switching to foreground `Agent` calls for the rest of the revision cycle — immediately produced direct, reliable results with no further manual pings needed.

**How to apply:** For any loop where you dispatch an agent, need its actual output to decide the next step, and the loop will repeat several times (spec/plan adversarial review, iterative fix-and-recheck cycles), default to foreground execution. Reserve background dispatch for genuinely fire-and-forget work or single dispatches where you have other useful work to do while waiting — not for a tight revise-review loop where you're doing nothing but waiting for the exact result anyway. If a background agent does go idle without delivering a report, proactively `SendMessage` a check-in rather than continuing to narrate "waiting" as a passive, confident state — and if the pattern recurs within the same loop, switch that loop to foreground rather than repeating the manual-ping workaround each round.

  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: ae412d01-e061-4047-918b-0d1df3d4d118
  modified: 2026-08-13T22:19:27.899Z
---

When running an iterative revise→re-check loop (e.g. canon-drafter ↔ canon-auditor, or vector-planner ↔ vector-challenger, cycling until a clean pass), dispatch each round's agent with `run_in_background: false` and wait for the direct result, rather than `run_in_background: true` and waiting for a task-notification.

**Why:** During the SPEC-APPLY-BATCH-002 ("Spec B", see [[project_manifest_persist_track]]) canon and vector review cycles, background-dispatched agents repeatedly went idle after finishing their work without proactively sending their final report — the only signal was a bare `idle_notification` with no content, requiring a manual `SendMessage` check-in to actually pull the result out. This happened for essentially every agent in the pipeline (verifier, auditor, drafter, exit-gate, planner, challenger) across dozens of rounds. The user noticed the pattern, called it out twice with increasing frustration ("The ui doesn't show any agents running", "You're full of shit", "Just rerun dammit"), and the fix — switching to foreground `Agent` calls for the rest of the revision cycle — immediately produced direct, reliable results with no further manual pings needed.

**How to apply:** For any loop where you dispatch an agent, need its actual output to decide the next step, and the loop will repeat several times (spec/plan adversarial review, iterative fix-and-recheck cycles), default to foreground execution. Reserve background dispatch for genuinely fire-and-forget work or single dispatches where you have other useful work to do while waiting — not for a tight revise-review loop where you're doing nothing but waiting for the exact result anyway. If a background agent does go idle without delivering a report, proactively `SendMessage` a check-in rather than continuing to narrate "waiting" as a passive, confident state — and if the pattern recurs within the same loop, switch that loop to foreground rather than repeating the manual-ping workaround each round.

`.claude/specs/SPEC-MANIFEST-PERSIST-001.json` ("Spec A") shipped 2026-08-13 (commits `7883c3b`..`d7ec596`, `fa73260`). `Manifest::persist` became a required trait method; `write_version`/`update_dependency_spec`/`update_optional_dependencies` do pure in-memory mutation only.

`.claude/specs/SPEC-APPLY-BATCH-002.json` ("Spec B") shipped 2026-08-14 (commits `d2b1014`..`c880280`, `c661b38`, `a739773`/`7346f48`). `apply_version_plan` now pre-scans a plan's Manifest-trait-routed writes via `classify_manifest_writes`, groups them per physical path, and opens/mutates/persists each path exactly once instead of once per bump/rewrite entry — the actual performance win the original audit finding was chasing.

**The scope decision that made Spec B safe:** the original combined spec died to a real data-loss ordering bug — a workspace root Cargo.toml can receive writes through both the `Manifest` trait (batchable) and the separate `WorkspaceCargoResolver` type (not batchable, does its own immediate mutate+persist), and naively batching the first while ignoring the second risks a stale in-memory snapshot clobbering the other's already-flushed write. Given three options (exclude mixed-routing paths from batching / reorder writes so the resolver always goes first / extend Spec A's mutate-persist split to `WorkspaceCargoResolver` too), the user picked the lowest-risk one: exclude. Any file touched by both mechanisms in one `apply_version_plan` call falls back entirely to today's unbatched, immediate per-entry behavior. This is a permanent scope boundary, not a stopgap — non_goals explicitly rejects both other options.

**How both specs got this rigorous:** Spec A's plan took 4 review rounds; Spec B's spec took 5 drafting/audit rounds (canon-exit-gate passed on retry 2) and its plan took 7 vector-challenger rounds. Real, substantive bugs were caught in nearly every round on both — see [[feedback_iterate_reviews_in_foreground]] for the operational lesson about how to run that many rounds without losing the user's confidence in what's actually running.

See also [[feedback_reviewer_must_actually_run_checks]] and [[feedback_canon_pipeline_scope]].

`git diff c736bbcfc8250c85f94c67919319c1814c5064db^ c736bbcfc8250c85f94c67919319c1814c5064db -- crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs | grep -E '^-' | grep -E 'ws_res\.(write_version|write_dependency)'` produced no output -- no removed or changed line touches a `ws_res.write_version`/`ws_res.write_dependency` call site. ## AC-017: bump-before-rewrites ordering is not byte-observable, correcting T13's commit-message evidence

T13's commit (`1234bef`) recorded a blanket claim that `CargoToml::update_dependency_spec` "only touches a dependency-table entry with a plan-time-constant value, no read of `current_version()`/other state." An independent review of that commit caught that this claim is incomplete for one branch, and since commit messages cannot be corrected after the fact, the complete evidence is recorded here instead.

Read `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs` directly:

- `CargoToml::write_version` (lines 200-242): touches only `[package].version` in the direct-write branch, or does an explicit pinned replacement of that same field for a workspace-inherited member. No other state is read or written. Claim holds without qualification.
- `CargoToml::update_dependency_spec` (lines 290-377): for a **non-inherited** dependency (lines 320-376, the case both of T13's AC-014/AC-016 fixtures and this file's own AC-005/AC-006 fixture exercise), the claim holds exactly as stated -- a disjoint dependency-table entry is mutated with a plan-time-constant `DepSpec`, no read of `current_version()`. For an **inherited** dependency (lines 305-318), the method instead delegates to `WorkspaceCargoResolver::load(&root_cargo)` followed by `ws_res.write_dependency(name, new, permit)` -- an immediate, synchronous read-and-persist against a **different physical file** (the workspace root `Cargo.toml`), not the manifest whose handle `update_dependency_spec` was called on. `WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_dependency` calls `self.persist(permit)` internally (cargo.rs:709), and `WorkspaceCargoResolver::persist` (cargo.rs:715-723) does not call `crate::record_persist_call()`, so this delegated write is invisible to `persist_call_count()`.

This does not weaken AC-017's actual claim: the delegated write lands on a file distinct from the one being batched in the group under discussion, so it has no bearing on whether bump-before-rewrites ordering is byte-observable *within that group's own manifest*. It also does not contradict this spec's own scope: `non_goals` already states that `WorkspaceCargoResolver`-routed writes remain immediate, per-entry, and outside `persist_call_count`'s instrumentation (which is scoped exclusively to the `Manifest` trait's three implementors). The correction here is one of completeness in T13's evidence write-up, not a functional defect in the shipped code -- verified via `cargo test -p callisto-graph --lib apply::tests` (22 passed) and `cargo clippy -p callisto-graph --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean) after this note was added, confirming no code change was needed or made.

# canon — Specification Skill

<overview>
canon turns requirements and research reports into unambiguous, testable specifications,
and turns defect class findings into architectural remediation specs. It enforces one
standard throughout: a developer who reads the output spec must be able to write an
implementation without asking a single clarifying question, and every acceptance
criterion must translate directly to a test case or type-level invariant check.
</overview>

---

<sub_skills>

### canon/draft
Given a `requirement@1` and optionally a `research-report@1`, produce a `spec@1` draft
with purpose, scope, non_goals, api_surface (if applicable), and acceptance criteria.
All criteria are testable propositions; error cases are covered with `is_error_case: true`.

### canon/verify
Given a draft `spec@1` plus the originating `requirement@1` and optional `research-report@1`, check whether each acceptance criterion is grounded in the source artifacts. Classifies criteria as supported, unsupported, or overfitted. Collects evidence only — does not produce a pass/fail verdict. Use this **before implementation** to confirm the spec is traceable to requirements.

### canon/drift
Given a spec@1 (via `spec_file_path`) and a workspace root, verify that the current code implements every acceptance criterion. Reads the spec from disk, reads the implementation from the workspace, and reports: `covered` (criterion is implemented and tested), `uncovered` (criterion has no matching implementation), and `drifted` (implementation exists but diverges from the criterion's contract). Use this **after implementation** to catch spec drift during maintenance — it is a diagnostic tool, not a blocking gate. lambda-exit-gate is the blocking gate; canon/drift is the ongoing health check.

### canon/audit
Given a `spec@1`, adversarially review it for untestable criteria, ambiguous language,
missing error cases, scope overlap, and incomplete sections. Returns a structured issue
list with specific rewritten suggested fixes.

### canon/gate
Given a `spec@1`, produce a binding pass/fail verdict before the spec enters planning. Default disposition is fail. On fail, returns specific blockers the drafter can act on without asking a follow-up question. On pass, the calling agent writes the spec to disk and sets `spec_file_path` — see the `<orchestration>` section.

### canon/architect
Given a `finding-report@1` from proof, produce a `spec@1` for the structural change that
eliminates the defect class — not a patch of individual instances but the abstraction
boundary, type invariant, or interface redesign that makes the class impossible to
reintroduce. This sub-skill closes the proof-to-design loop.

</sub_skills>

---

<artifact_contracts>

**Consumes**: `requirement@1`, `research-report@1` (optional), `finding-report@1` (canon/architect only), `spec_file_path` + workspace root (canon/drift only)

**Produces**: `spec@1` (written to `.claude/specs/<id>.json` by the skill orchestrator after gate pass; `spec_file_path` set to the workspace-relative path), `verdict@1` (canon/gate only)

</artifact_contracts>

---

<pipeline>

**Standard drafting pipeline:**
```
requirement@1 [+ research-report@1]
  → canon-drafter          (returns spec object — no disk write)
  → canon-verifier         (grounding check against source artifacts)
  → canon-auditor          (adversarial quality review)
  → canon-exit-gate        (binding pass/fail verdict)
  → [skill writes .claude/specs/<id>.json, sets spec_file_path]
  → spec@1
```

**On-demand drift pipeline (maintenance, any time after implementation):**
```
spec_file_path + workspace root
  → canon-drift-checker
  → drift report (covered / uncovered / drifted)
```

**Architectural remediation pipeline (invoked after proof):**
```
finding-report@1
  → canon-architect
  → canon-exit-gate
  → spec@1 (architectural)
  → vector → lambda
```

`canon-architect` is not part of the standard drafting pipeline. It is invoked when
proof returns a `finding-report@1` and the root cause requires a structural fix. The
output spec feeds back into vector for planning.

</pipeline>

---

<orchestration>

After `canon-exit-gate` returns a pass verdict, the calling agent MUST perform this step before handing off to vector:

1. Write the spec@1 JSON to `<workspace_root>/.claude/specs/<id>.json` using the file writing tool. Create the directory if it does not exist.
2. Set `spec_file_path` to the workspace-relative path (e.g. `.claude/specs/SPEC-001.json`) in the spec@1 object.
3. Pass the updated spec@1 — with `spec_file_path` set — to vector-planner.

This step is not optional. Without `spec_file_path` set, downstream agents fall back to reading the spec from conversation context, which is lossy under compression and cannot be independently verified.

</orchestration>

---

<framework_references>
- [Agent Best Practices](../../../shared/agent-best-practices.md)
- [Spec Schema](../../../shared/schemas/spec@1.json)
- [Verdict Schema](../../../shared/schemas/verdict@1.json)
- [Finding Report Schema](../../../shared/schemas/finding-report@1.json)
</framework_references>

---

<subagent_dispatch_matrix>

| Agent | Sub-skill | When to Delegate |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`canon-drafter`** | draft | Producing a new spec from a requirement or research report. |
| **`canon-verifier`** | verify | Checking that each acceptance criterion is grounded in the source artifacts (pre-implementation only). |
| **`canon-drift-checker`** | drift | On-demand post-implementation drift check: reads spec from disk, reads code, classifies criteria as covered / uncovered / drifted. |
| **`canon-auditor`** | audit | Adversarial quality review for untestable language, ambiguity, and missing error cases. |
| **`canon-exit-gate`** | gate | Binding pass/fail judgment before handing the spec to planning. |
| **`canon-architect`** | architect | Designing the structural fix for a defect class surfaced by proof. |

</subagent_dispatch_matrix>


ARGUMENTS: Draft a spec for: apply_version_plan performance/architecture fix (Track: Manifest write-batching).

Requirement:
- crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs's apply_version_plan currently opens, reads, and parses a manifest file fresh (callisto_manifests::open) for EVERY entry in plan.bumps and plan.rewrites that targets it, and each of those calls Manifest::write_version / Manifest::update_dependency_spec internally persists (atomic_write: temp file + rename + fsync parent + fsync grandparent) on every single call. When N bumps/rewrites target the same file (e.g. an app crate depending on 5 sibling packages that bump together, all rewriting app/Cargo.toml's dependency table), this costs N full read+parse+write+2-fsync cycles on one file instead of 1.
- Confirmed via code reading: crates/callisto-manifests/src/{cargo,npm,python}.rs each implement the Manifest trait's write_version/update_dependency_spec/update_optional_dependencies by mutating an in-memory doc and then calling a private `fn persist(&mut self, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), ManifestError>` at the end of every one of those methods.
- Fix requires: (1) restructure the Manifest trait (crates/callisto-manifests/src/lib.rs) so write_version/update_dependency_spec/update_optional_dependencies perform ONLY the in-memory mutation (no disk I/O), and expose persist as its own trait method the caller invokes explicitly; (2) apply.rs's apply_version_plan must group plan.bumps' writes and plan.rewrites by their resolved target path BEFORE looping, open each distinct path's manifest exactly once, apply every mutation destined for that path against the same open handle, then call persist() exactly once per file.
- Constraints to respect: CLAUDE.md invariant #2 (format preservation via CST editors) must hold across multiple in-memory mutations before the single persist. unsafe_code = "forbid" (workspace-wide). Must not silently change existing callers' expectations without updating them.
- Known blast radius to inventory precisely during spec/plan: ~28 existing call sites of write_version/update_dependency_spec/update_optional_dependencies inside crates/callisto-manifests/src/{cargo,npm,python}.rs's own #[cfg(test)] modules -- many read the manifest file back from disk immediately after calling one of these methods to assert on-disk content; each such test will need an explicit `.persist(&permit)` call added after its mutation(s) once auto-persist is removed. apply.rs itself is the only external (non-test) caller of these three methods anywhere in the workspace (confirmed via grep).
- Explicit design decision needed and must be captured as a testable acceptance criterion: partial-failure/atomicity semantics change. Today, if bump 3-of-5 fails validation (e.g. UnexpectedManifestVersion) mid-loop, bumps 1-2 have ALREADY been persisted to disk (partial application). After batching (mutate-all-in-memory-then-persist-once-per-file), a failure during in-memory mutation for a given file would mean NOTHING for that file gets persisted (that file's batch is all-or-nothing), while files whose batches completed successfully before the failing one would still be persisted (across-file atomicity is unchanged; per-file atomicity improves to all-or-nothing). This must be stated explicitly in the spec's acceptance criteria, not left implicit, and needs its own test.
- Out of scope: do not touch changelog writes, consumed-changeset deletion, pre.json write, or lockfile refresh logic in apply.rs -- only the plan.bumps (VersionWriteTarget::Manifest paths) and plan.rewrites (DepWriteTarget::Manifest paths) loops that currently call open()+write_version/update_dependency_spec per-entry. CargoWorkspacePackage/CargoWorkspaceDependency write targets (which go through WorkspaceCargoResolver, a different type, not the Manifest trait) are also out of scope for this track unless investigation shows they have the identical redundant-open problem -- check and note in the spec's scope section either way.

Workspace root: /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto. Relevant files to read: crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs, crates/callisto-manifests/src/lib.rs (Manifest trait definition), crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs, crates/callisto-manifests/src/npm.rs, crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/plan.rs (VersionPlan/PlannedBump/SpecRewrite/VersionWriteTarget/DepWriteTarget shapes).
